problem.name: Fixed-subgraph containment
problem.statement_latex: Fix a nonempty graph $H$ with $k$ vertices, $m$ edges and a vertex of degree $d$. Given adjacency queries to an $n$-vertex graph $G$, decide whether $G$ contains a subgraph isomorphic to $H$.
problem.statement_text: Fix a nonempty graph $H$ with $k$ vertices, $m$ edges and a vertex of degree $d$. Given adjacency queries to an $n$-vertex graph $G$, decide whether $G$ contains a subgraph isomorphic to $H$.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(n^{2-2/k-t})$ queries by Lee--Magniez--Santha learning graphs, where $t=\max\{(k^2-2(m+1))/(k(k+1)(m+1)),(2k-d-3)/(k(d+1)(m-d+2))\}$. The pattern is constant-sized.
quantum.headline_text: $O(n^{2-2/k-t})$ queries by Lee–Magniez–Santha learning graphs, where $t=\max\{(k^2-2(m+1))/(k(k+1)(m+1)),(2k-d-3)/(k(d+1)(m-d+2))\}$. The pattern is constant-sized.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(n^2)$ randomized adjacency queries in the worst case; after acquiring the matrix, classical subgraph algorithms perform the computation.
